caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
The counts come from Salmon with no record of whether the length correction was applied; state this in the QC output as an unresolved provenance caveat.

plan.title: Hallmark signature scores: CD inflamed ileum vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12000 x 12 gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv) with a 12-row sample table (metadata.csv) describing 6 Crohn disease inflamed ileum samples versus 6 controls, unpaired, single batch. The research question asks for a score per hallmark signature per sample plus a test of which signatures differ between inflamed and control, and flags one shallow library (sample_01, ~4x below median). The plan follows that literally and adds nothing else.

T1S1 establishes sample structure before any scoring: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and a library-size/detected-gene table with sample_01 marked. Per the low-depth rule the shallow sample is kept and inspected, not deleted silently; if the QC gives a concrete reason beyond depth alone (e.g. it separates from both groups on PCA), the step states that reason and the scoring step is repeated with and without it as a sensitivity check. T1S2 filters genes to >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size) and produces median-of-ratios size factors and a log-normalized (VST / log2 normalized-count) matrix as the scoring input; no pre-scaling of counts before size-factor estimation. Because the count table is Salmon output with an unrecorded length correction, T1S2 states this and treats the counts as gene-level counts for size-factor normalization, noting the caveat.

T3S1 scores all 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets per sample with UCell, a rank-based per-sample method whose ranks are insensitive to sequencing depth — the right choice given the shallow sample. It then tests each signature score between inflamed and control with limma on the score matrix under the ~ condition design, BH-adjusted across the 50 signatures, and reports for each set the number of member genes actually present in the 12000-gene matrix along with the collection source and version. Only 12 samples means only 12 units per test, so the power statement is part of the output, not an afterthought. T1S3 assembles the score matrix, the per-signature test table, the QC figures, and a reproducibility record.

The human hallmark GMT is present in the reference store; the step must confirm its presence at run time and report the collection version alongside the scores.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size table
keep genes with >=10 counts in at least smallest group size samples; median-of-ratios size factors
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample on MSigDB hallmark sets
